title: Per-tenant Throughput Targets and Fail-safe Scaling Engine
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated customers expect firm throughput guarantees and predictable latency under spiky traffic. Current autoscaler reacts to node-level metrics and global pool utilization but lacks per-tenant target propagation, pacing on warm KV caches, and a coordinated fail-safe that enforces SLOs without causing runaway scale. This ticket defines a policy engine design and implementation plan to support per-tenant throughput targets, multiple scaling algorithms (proactive, reactive, and hybrid), and bounded safety limits that protect platform capacity and cost objectives.

Goals:
- Add per-tenant target metrics that can be expressed as throughput (requests/sec), token/sec, and P95 latency budget.
- Provide three selectable algorithms: conservative reactive (metric threshold-driven), predictive (short-term ML forecast + capacitive reserve), and hybrid (reactive with predictive cooldowns).
- Implement safety limits: min/max instance bounds, burst budget, cooldown windows, and cross-tenant override that prevents a single tenant from starving others.
- Expose policy configuration via the Dedicated API and Console, with audit logging and rollout flags.

Non-goals: automatic capacity purchases; internal autoscaler refactor beyond the policy layer; per-request scheduling changes (left to runtime).
proposal:
High-level approach:
1) Policy model: introduce a lightweight policy resource attached to each dedicated tenant (tenant_policy_id) describing target_metric_type, target_value, algorithm, and safety_limits. Policy is stored in control plane and evaluated by the autoscale controller at regular intervals (control tick).
2) Metrics mapping: translate tenant-level objectives to the autoscaler input: requests/sec -> desired_instances using per-instance throughput profiles; tokens/sec -> per-model token-rate conversion table; latency budgets -> headroom margins applied to desired_instances.
3) Algorithms:
  - Reactive: sliding-window metric aggregation, quantile thresholds, and proportional-additive scaling steps (min step = 1 instance, max step = 25% of current fleet).
  - Predictive: short-horizon ARIMA-lite/ExponentialSmoothing ensemble trained on 5-min windows, fallback to reactive when forecast confidence low.
  - Hybrid: reactive baseline with predictive cooldowns to delay downscales and pre-warm capacity before anticipated spikes.
4) Safety limits: per-tenant hard max, cluster-wide soft cap, emergency backpressure signal to reject or degrade low-priority routes when cluster saturation detected.
5) Observability: per-policy time-series (desired_instances, actual_instances, forecast, safety_triggers) + alert rules for repeated oscillation or safety-limit hits.

Implementation notes: keep policy evaluation idempotent and deterministic; prefer integer math for instance computations; use existing autoscaler leader instance to avoid split-brain; persist decisions for audit and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Policy resource schema defined and migrated (DB migration and API surface documented)
Autoscaler consumes per-tenant policy and emits desired_instances metric per control tick
Three algorithms implemented behind feature flags and validated with synthetic load tests
Safety limits enforced: attempts to exceed hard max are blocked and logged; cluster soft cap triggers degradation route
Console UI shows policy status and time-series; API accepts updates and returns validation errors
End-to-end benchmark: simulated tenant with 10x traffic spike meets P95 latency budget 95% of the time under constrained cluster (within safety limits)
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for scaling math, cooldown windows, and safety-limit gating
Integration test harness that replays historic production traffic traces against a scaled-down cluster simulator
Chaos tests: leader failover during control tick and network partition between control plane and nodes
Canary rollout: start with 3 internal tenants, then 10 pilot customers before wide release
Cost regression test to measure delta in instance-hours across algorithms
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged merge behind autoscale-policy-v2 flag. 2) Enable reactive algorithm for small internal tenants (flag=true). 3) Run 48h soak with synthetic spiky traffic and monitor oscillation alerts. 4) Enable predictive for selected pilot tenants with telemetry on forecast confidence. 5) Gradually allow hybrid for tenants that opt-in via Console. 6) After 2 weeks of healthy signals, flip default for new Dedicated tenants. 7) Post-mortem & tuning cycle.
migration_steps:
- DB migration: add tenant_policy table and default policies for existing tenants.
- Backfill: set default conservative reactive policies for all active dedicated tenants.
- Config: add API v1.1 endpoint for policy CRUD; Console form for policy editing with validation.
- Rollback: revert flag and remove policy evaluator from leader loop; keep data intact for re-enabling.
open_decisions: How to map tokens/sec to instances reliably across heterogeneous model mixes (per-model profiling vs tenant-level estimation)
Exact forecast model to use in Predictive algorithm (start simple and iterate), and model training cadence/feature set
Policy ownership UX: should Console allow raw numeric edits or only presets (conservative/balanced/aggressive)?
Cross-tenant eviction policy when cluster soft cap reached — should we degrade routes or apply probabilistic request shedding?
